trap-superlative.notes: STANDING-TRAP FINDINGS, report only. (1) ARITHMETIC: 'Vol(B_3)/Vol(5_2) approx 2.592' is wrong in the last digit. Recomputed at mpmath dps=30 with Vol(B_3) = 8G = 7.32772475342 and Vol(5_2) = 2.82812208833: the ratio is 2.591021365, which rounds to 2.591. The companion ratio Vol(B_3)/Vol(4_1) = 3.609924309 is correct as 3.610. (2) LOGIC, the closing sentence: 'Linear independence is strictly weaker than algebraic independence but STRICTLY STRONGER THAN IRRATIONALITY.' The second half is false as stated. Q-linear independence of {V_1, V_2, V_3} does not imply any V_i is irrational - counterexample {1, sqrt 2, sqrt 3}, which is Q-linearly independent while its first element is rational. Irrationality of V_1 is Q-linear independence of {1, V_1}, and 1 is not in the set. Proposed fix: state the conjecture for the four-element set {1, Vol(4_1), Vol(5_2), Vol(B_3)}, under which the comparison to conj:single-volume-irrationality does hold. (3) ARGUMENT GAP: the non-commensurability of B_3 is argued from 'its cusp geometry is incompatible with the knot complements' plus the two volume ratios 'confirming the link volume is not a simple rational multiple'. A numerical ratio to four digits cannot establish irrationality, and the block already has the clean argument available - the Borromean complement is arithmetic over Q(i) while 4_1 is arithmetic over Q(sqrt -3), so their invariant trace fields differ and they cannot be commensurable. Using the ratios instead leaves the strongest of the three cases resting on the weakest evidence.
